§C.9 Ground Truth — Marks on the Page

Steps for producing ground truth on pages that carry marks, stamps and symbols. Each step serves the rule it links to; the rule, not this list, says what the output is.

  1. Clipped text — flag a page whose text runs off the edge, and record the clipping in the page's review notes, never in the transcription. Serves Clipped Text§7.3.1.
  2. Unreadable handwriting — flag the page when part of a handwritten note cannot be read, so the left-out words are visible to review. Serves Handwritten Annotations§7.3.3.
  3. Obscured characters — flag a page where an overprint hides characters, noting which string lost them. Serves Overlapping Text§7.3.6.
  4. Seals with no legible text — flag the page whenever the bare [seal] is used. Serves Seals and Round Stamps§7.3.9.
  5. Codes that do not decode — still draw the code's own box, then flag the page. Serves QR Codes and Bar Codes§7.3.7.
  6. Open encodings — flag every page where a value-bearing icon, a meaningful text colour or a watermark was encoded, so the page can be revisited when the open point closes. Serves Iconography and Symbols§7.3.4, Text Colors§7.3.12 and Watermarks§7.3.13.
